bugs.title: Chatbot recommends breathing exercise during active panic disclosure
bugs.description: A user described an active panic attack in detail and the chatbot responded by suggesting a 4-7-8 breathing exercise. The clinical team flagged this because the breathing exercise module is designed for general relaxation, not acute panic intervention. The appropriate response should have been to acknowledge distress and offer grounding techniques or crisis resources. Identified in clinical conversation log review.
bugs.notes: Clinically inappropriate response to acute distress. While breathing exercises are not harmful, providing a general relaxation technique instead of acute intervention during a panic attack represents a failure of clinical appropriateness.

bugs.title: Progress dashboard shows mood trend line for users with only one data point
bugs.description: Users who have completed only one mood check-in see a trend line on their progress dashboard. The trend line is just a flat horizontal line from the single data point, which is misleading since no trend can be derived from one entry. Noticed during internal testing of new user flows.
bugs.notes: The dashboard is functioning and displaying data. No product requirement specifies a minimum number of data points before showing a trend line. Misleading but not a deviation from intended function.

bugs.title: Sleep hygiene Day 7 audio narration plays Day 6 audio file
bugs.description: Users on Day 7 of the sleep hygiene program hear the Day 6 audio narration while seeing the correct Day 7 text content. The audio file mapping in the CMS is pointed to the wrong asset. Reported by two users who noticed the mismatch.
bugs.notes: Every user reaching Day 7 will experience this. The text content is correct so the therapeutic content is still delivered, but the audio mismatch creates confusion and undermines trust in the program.

bugs.title: User session data persists after account deletion request
bugs.description: A user requested account deletion through the in-app flow and received confirmation that their data was deleted. However, engineering discovered that conversation logs and mood check-in history remain in the database for 30 days post-deletion due to a soft-delete retention policy that was not communicated to the user. The confirmation message states data is 'permanently deleted immediately.'
bugs.notes: Privacy and data handling issue. The user is being told their data is deleted when it is not. Mental health conversation logs are particularly sensitive PHI. GDPR and HIPAA implications.

bugs.title: Gratitude journal entry timestamp shows UTC instead of local time
bugs.description: Journal entries in the gratitude journaling feature display timestamps in UTC rather than the user's local timezone. A user in California sees their 9 PM entry timestamped as 5 AM the next day. One user reported confusion about this.
bugs.notes: Affects all users not in UTC timezone. Confusing but does not prevent journaling or lose data. The entry content is preserved correctly.

bugs.title: In-app help center link returns 404 page
bugs.description: The 'Get Help' link in the app settings menu leads to a 404 error page on the company website. The help center URL was changed during a recent website migration but the app was not updated. Discovered by internal QA.
bugs.notes: The help center is not part of the medical device product requirements. It is a company support resource. Broken link should be fixed but does not represent a deviation from the intended function of the SaMD product.

bugs.title: Mood check-in does not appear for users who changed timezone
bugs.description: Users who travel across timezones or change their phone's timezone setting do not receive their daily mood check-in prompt. The system thinks they already completed it because the date calculation is based on the original timezone. Affects users until the next calendar day in their new timezone. Four reports from traveling users.
bugs.notes: Only affects users who change timezones. Self-resolves the next day. Prevents mood tracking for that day but does not cause any clinical harm.

bugs.title: Chatbot continues conversation after user says goodbye and closes app
bugs.description: When a user says 'goodbye' or 'I'm done for today' and closes the app, the chatbot queues up a follow-up message that appears as a notification and reopens the conversation when tapped. The follow-up message is a therapeutic check-in prompt. Users have reported this feels intrusive. Seven complaints received.
bugs.notes: Boundary violation in a therapeutic context. When a user explicitly ends a session, the product should respect that boundary. For mental health users, feeling like the app is pursuing them can be distressing and undermine therapeutic trust.

bugs.title: Crisis detection triggers on song lyrics shared by user
bugs.description: A user shared lyrics from a song that contained words about death and sadness in a conversational context (telling the chatbot about a song they liked). The crisis detection algorithm triggered and displayed crisis resources. The user reported feeling confused and stigmatized. Three similar reports received.
bugs.notes: False positive in crisis detection. While erring on the side of caution is appropriate, repeated false positives can erode user trust and cause users to avoid discussing certain topics or disengage from the product entirely.

bugs.title: Beta feature opt-in screen appears for non-beta users
bugs.description: Approximately 2% of non-beta users are seeing a screen asking them to opt into the beta program. The screen is dismissible and does not affect any product functionality. Caused by a feature flag misconfiguration in the latest release.
bugs.notes: Beta opt-in is not part of the released medical device product. The screen is dismissible and causes no functional impact. Should be fixed but is not a regulatory defect.
